blocks.text: Day 2 · A city tour of Quito, founded in the 16th century on the ruins of an Inca city at about 2,850 m: one of the best-preserved historic centres in Latin America, a showcase of the Quito School of Art and among the very first sites inscribed on UNESCO’s World Heritage List. See the Plaza Grande with the Cathedral, the Presidential Palace and City Hall, the Jesuit church of La Compañía, the neo-Gothic Basílica del Voto Nacional, inspired by Notre-Dame de Paris, with its gargoyles shaped like Ecuadorian animals, and the view from El Panecillo. In the afternoon, the TelefériQo rises in 20 minutes from 2,950 to about 4,000 m, and a short walk up Cruz Loma crosses the páramo, with views of Cotopaxi, Antisana and Cayambe on clear days. Overnight at Patio Andaluz 4★. (B, box lunch)

blocks.text: Day 3 · North to Imbabura: chirimoya in Guayllabamba, a family making the traditional bizcochos and layered cheese of Cayambe (coffee break included), the Miralago viewpoint over Imbabura Volcano and Lake San Pablo, and the Plaza de los Ponchos in Otavalo, one of the largest Indigenous markets in South America. Continue to Cotacachi, famous for its leather goods, and the sacred Peguche Waterfall, through a eucalyptus forest. Overnight at Hacienda Pinsaqui. (B)
